title: Econ tuning initiative: batching, caching, and quantization roadmap tracker
creator: Nora Patel
description: This initiative coordinates cross-functional work to reduce per-token inference costs 20-30% across typical Redwood workloads by targeting batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization strategies. The ticket tracks roadmap milestones, success metrics, experiments, and rollout gates for Dedicated and Hosted customers.
background: Cost per-token is a top customer objection in sales cycles and a key internal OKR for 2025 Q2. Prior experiments show batching & cache can reduce tokens billed by up to 25% for request distributions with repeated prefixes; quantization experiments affect latency and quality trade-offs. We need an initiative-level tracker that ties experiments to OKRs, exposes dashboards, and coordinates rollout timelines between runtime, infra, SDKs, and Console teams.
objectives: Reduce normalized tokens-per-dollar by 20% for text-generation workloads
Raise average KV cache hit rate to >= 40% in production for long-context chat workloads
Implement two quantization profiles validated against quality thresholds for low-cost tiers
key_results: rollout_coverage: 80% of Hosted traffic using optimized profiles by EOD 2025-06-30
milestones: M1: benchmarking suite and synthetic workloads ready - 2025-03-15
M2: batching autoscaler + SDK changes merged - 2025-04-10
M3: KV cache policy opt-in beta - 2025-05-01
M5: staged rollout and metric validation - 2025-06-15
risks_and_mitigation: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization - mitigation: gated A/B with automated eval harness and rollback
Increased tail latency from batching - mitigation: latency SLO bump for critical routes and dynamic batching thresholds
Customer billing confusion from cache effects - mitigation: Console billing rework and docs + gradual opt-in
plan_of_record: Phase 0: instrumentation & baselining (Mar 2025) - collect tokens-per-request, seq length histograms, prefix repetition metrics
Phase 1: experiments (Apr-May 2025) - run controlled A/B for batching, KV policies, and 8-bit/4-bit quant profiles
Phase 2: rollout (Jun 2025) - canary targeting low-risk tenants, monitor offline quality, billing, latency
Phase 3: expand & iterate (Jul-Sep 2025) - wider rollout, additional model profiles, Dedicated capacity opt-in paths
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks show >=20% tokens-per-dollar reduction on representative workloads
No customer-facing quality regression > 2% on evaluation prompts
Console shows correct cost attribution for cached requests
Operational runbook and rollback path documented and tested
open_questions: Should we make KV caching on by default for Hosted customers or opt-in during beta?
Do we expose quantization profile selection in the API, or keep it runtime-controlled?
What SLO delta are we willing to accept for batched routes?
